mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the addition theorem for two events A and B?

options.A: P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A \cap B)
options.C: P(A \cup B) = P(A) – P(B) + P(A \cap B)

mcqs.answer: P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) – P(A \cap B)
mcqs.explanation: The addition theorem states that the probability of the union of two events equals the sum of their individual probabilities minus the probability of their intersection, to avoid double‑counting the overlap. Option A is the correct formulation; the other options either omit the intersection term or use incorrect operations.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate probability of A union B
mcqs.question: If P(A)=0.3, P(B)=0.5 and P(A\cap B)=0.1, what is P(A\cup B)?
mcqs.explanation: Using the addition theorem: P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)=0.3+0.5-0.1=0.7. The other options result from incorrect addition or subtraction.

mcqs.question: Which pair of events is mutually exclusive?

options.A: Rolling a 2 and rolling an even number on a single die
options.B: Drawing a heart and drawing a spade from a standard deck of cards
options.C: Getting a head and getting a tail on the same toss of a fair coin
options.D: Selecting a red card and selecting a king from a deck of cards

mcqs.answer: Getting a head and getting a tail on the same toss of a fair coin
mcqs.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together. In a single coin toss, obtaining a head and a tail simultaneously is impossible, so they are mutually exclusive. Options A, B, and D can occur together (e.g., a 2 is even, a card can be both red and a king).

mcqs.learning_point: Apply the theorem to numerical problems
mcqs.question: A bag contains 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green balls. One ball is drawn at random. Let A be the event "the ball is red" and B be the event "the ball is blue". What is P(A\cup B)?
mcqs.explanation: A and B are mutually exclusive (a ball cannot be both red and blue). Hence P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=5/12+4/12=9/12. Option C is correct; the other options either ignore one of the events or incorrectly add the total number of balls.

mcqs.question: A student claims that for any two events A and B, P(A\cup B) = P(A) + P(B). Which statement correctly addresses this misconception?

options.A: The claim is always true because probabilities simply add.
options.B: The claim is false; we must subtract P(A\cap B) to avoid double counting.
options.C: The claim is false; we must add P(A\cap B) instead of subtracting.
options.D: The claim is true only when A and B are independent.

mcqs.answer: The claim is false; we must subtract P(A\cap B) to avoid double counting.
mcqs.explanation: The addition theorem requires subtracting the intersection probability to correct for the overlap. Option B states this precisely. Option A ignores the overlap, Option C suggests the opposite operation, and Option D confuses independence with mutual exclusivity.

mcqs.learning_point: Calculate probability of A union B
mcqs.question: If P(A)=0.4, P(B)=0.6 and A and B are mutually exclusive, what is P(A\cup B)?
mcqs.explanation: For mutually exclusive events, P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)=0.4+0.6=1.0. The other options result from incorrect subtraction or misunderstanding of mutual exclusivity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes mutually exclusive events from independent events?

options.A: Mutually exclusive events can occur together, while independent events cannot.
options.B: For mutually exclusive events, P(A\cap B)=0; for independent events, P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B).
options.C: Mutually exclusive events always have P(A)=P(B); independent events always have P(A)=P(B).
options.D: If events are mutually exclusive they are also independent.

mcqs.answer: For mutually exclusive events, P(A\cap B)=0; for independent events, P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B).
mcqs.explanation: Mutually exclusive events never occur together, so their intersection probability is zero. Independent events have no influence on each other, so the intersection probability equals the product of their individual probabilities. Option B captures both definitions correctly; the other options are false statements.

mcqs.learning_point: Apply the theorem to numerical problems
mcqs.question: Two fair dice are rolled. Let A be the event "the sum of the dice is 7" and B be the event "at least one die shows a 4". What is P(A\cup B)?
mcqs.explanation: Total outcomes = 36. |A|=6 (sum 7). |B|=11 (at least one 4). |A∩B|=2 ((3,4) and (4,3)). Using the addition theorem: P(A\cup B) = (6+11-2)/36 = 15/36 = 5/12. Option A matches this value; the other options are results of miscounting the intersection or using incorrect totals.
